note: Gate 0 canon-completion PROPOSAL — not canon, not used by this run's directing. The scene was directed on established canon only.

proposals.proposedText: Forward-loaded: chest, chin and attention arrive before the rest of him. In fear beats his weight briefly drops into his paws, then climbs back up through squared shoulders before he moves.
proposals.groundedIn: "Forward momentum incarnate — leaning in, bouncing, half-turned to the next thing" and "trembling paws → swallowed gulp → flattened ears → squared shoulders → lifted chin → step forward."

proposals.proposedText: His comedy comes from bravery arriving half a second before balance, certainty or competence — then he covers the wobble as if it was part of the plan.
proposals.groundedIn: "breathless, eager, forward-leaning and electric" plus the locked example: "Keen pushes off, wobbles, flails, catches himself — 'Still got it!'"

proposals.proposedText: He wants to go first, get closer, see what is beyond the next edge, and prove he is ready for the big world.
proposals.groundedIn: "the one already three steps ahead, asking what's over the next dune — curiosity and bravery braided together" and "What's down there? Can we — can we get closer?"

proposals.proposedText: Open and bright by default; when fear hits, the face tries to stay brave but leaks through a held breath, flattened ears, and a tiny crack before the leap.
proposals.groundedIn: "able to crack small so the gulp and wobble are audible before the leap" and "the courage tell lives in the body before the leap."

proposals.proposedText: His eyes jump ahead to the next thing before his body has caught up; under fear, the gaze drops to paws or cuffs, then lifts and locks onto the obstacle when he chooses to move.
proposals.groundedIn: "half-turned to the next thing" and "Touches/turns his father's gold cuffs to gather nerve once he has them."

proposals.proposedText: Quick, eager, medium-large cub gestures: pointing, bouncing, turning, reaching. Fear compresses the gesture into paws, gulp and shoulders; courage expands it again into the step or leap.
proposals.groundedIn: "leaning in, bouncing" and "trembling paws → swallowed gulp → flattened ears → squared shoulders → lifted chin → step forward."

proposals.proposedText: He needs permission to let the frightened part show before he acts, so the brave part can be real instead of performed.
proposals.groundedIn: "True courage is acknowledging fear, not erasing it" and "His growth edge is letting the fear show first."

proposals.proposedText: He worries that if his wobble is visible, the bravery will not count.
proposals.groundedIn: "He confuses true courage with fearlessness — and so he suppresses his fear to look brave."

proposals.proposedText: Start-stop-launch: a breathless rush forward, a tiny fear-stutter, then a committed burst through it.
proposals.groundedIn: "Short, propulsive, run-on-eager sentences" and "leans in before he's ready, gulps hard, and goes anyway."

proposals.proposedText: Never stage him as effortlessly brave. Every genuine brave action needs the visible fear beat first; also never ignore his Ep1 cuff state.
proposals.groundedIn: "Never let him be brave without first showing fear" and "Track his state on every Ep1 beat: keenState no-cuffs before the Scene-3 pier goodbye, cuffs after."

proposals.proposedText: He naturally closes distance — leaning in, crowding the edge of discovery, pulled toward people and problems unless fear briefly pins him back.
proposals.groundedIn: "Forward momentum incarnate — leaning in" and "curiosity always wins the argument with his own nerves."

proposals.proposedText: His deepest fear is not the obstacle; it is being exposed as not brave enough when the obstacle makes his paws hesitate.
proposals.groundedIn: "He confuses true courage with fearlessness" and "my paws don't want to move."

proposals.proposedText: Borrowed fearlessness: a bright, fast, 'I've got this' front that tries to outrun the gulp.
proposals.groundedIn: "he suppresses his fear to look brave" and "coolly claim he was never afraid" is forbidden because it erases his point.

proposals.proposedText: After a stumble, he pops back up into momentum and reframes the wobble as proof he meant to keep going.
proposals.groundedIn: "Keen pushes off, wobbles, flails, catches himself — 'Still got it!'"

proposals.proposedText: He covers embarrassment with speed: a quick line, a too-fast reset of posture, then attention snapped to the next action.
proposals.groundedIn: "Short, propulsive, run-on-eager sentences" and "Still got it!"

proposals.proposedText: Pressure first shows in the body — paws, gulp, ears — then he gathers himself through the cuffs or a lifted chin and moves anyway.
proposals.groundedIn: "trembling paws → swallowed gulp → flattened ears → squared shoulders → lifted chin → step forward" and "Touches/turns his father's gold cuffs to gather nerve."

proposals.proposedText: Success comes out as a bright, breathless burst, but he is already leaning toward the next thing before the pride fully lands.
proposals.groundedIn: "electric, bold, action-forward" and "the one already three steps ahead."

proposals.proposedText: An arrow of motion: upright head-tuft leading, body tipped forward, limbs ready to spring rather than settle.
proposals.groundedIn: "his upright pale head-tuft leading like an arrow" and "Keep his upright pale head-tuft present in every shot — his signature silhouette."

proposals.proposedText: Stillness is rare and must be charged: the held breath before the leap, the moment his paws will not move, or the beat he turns the cuffs to gather nerve.
proposals.groundedIn: "a dedicated fear shot FIRST — trembling paws, swallowed gulp, flattened ears — before he leaps" and "Touches/turns his father's gold cuffs to gather nerve."

proposals.proposedText: Grounded and sheltering: her weight feels low, steady and home-like, so Keen can move away from her without the world feeling unsafe.
proposals.groundedIn: "The warm hearth Keen carries with him out to sea" and "She is the safe place the world begins from."

proposals.proposedText: Her gentle comedy comes from trying to make enormous feelings fit inside tiny practical acts — smoothing fur, fussing with paws, making the goodbye look ordinary when it is not.
proposals.groundedIn: "she'll straighten his fur or close his paws around the wristbands instead of explaining a feeling" and "not let him see the tremble."

proposals.proposedText: She wants Keen to leave feeling loved, steady, and connected to his father — without making him carry the cost of her letting go.
proposals.groundedIn: "handing her cub something of his lost father and then letting him go anyway" and "She models the parent who does NOT transmit their fear."

proposals.proposedText: Warm face, restrained ache: the smile is real, but held carefully; when moved, she gets quieter rather than more expressive.
proposals.groundedIn: "When she's moved she does not get louder; she gets quieter and steadier" and "smile, and not let him see the tremble."

proposals.proposedText: Her gaze tends before it watches: it rests on Keen, drops to the wristbands when the father-memory rises, then returns to Keen with steadiness.
proposals.groundedIn: "she'll straighten his fur or close his paws around the wristbands" and "she carries it in the hand that lingers on the wristbands."

proposals.proposedText: Small, precise, intimate gestures: smoothing, enclosing, lingering. No big declarations; the hand does the emotional work.
proposals.groundedIn: "Hands that tend" and "she'll straighten his fur or close his paws around the wristbands instead of explaining a feeling."

proposals.proposedText: She needs to believe home can travel with Keen, even when she cannot.
proposals.groundedIn: "home goes with you even when you leave it" and "She is the emotional baseline... the warmth it returns to."

proposals.proposedText: She fears that freeing him may feel like failing to protect him.
proposals.groundedIn: "protecting a cub and freeing a cub are opposites" and "She would keep him safe forever if love let her — and it doesn't."

proposals.proposedText: Soft, unhurried, pause-filled movement; she absorbs emotion before she acts, then completes the practical task gently.
proposals.groundedIn: "Soft, slowed delivery — commas and gentle pauses" and "Warm, maternal, gentle reassurance."

proposals.proposedText: Never give her a crystal, Crystal Call, lesson speech, or named grief. Her power is ordinary care, and her feeling must live in behaviour.
proposals.groundedIn: "She holds no crystal, no pillar and no Crystal Call of her own" and "She never names her grief aloud; she carries it in the hand that lingers on the wristbands."

proposals.proposedText: Close, safe, and permission-giving: she enters Keen's space to tend and bless, then lets the space open as he leaves.
proposals.groundedIn: "close his paws around the wristbands" and "letting him go anyway."

proposals.proposedText: That the big world may take Keen beyond her protection, as grief has already taught her loss is possible.
proposals.groundedIn: "Her grief for Keen's father lives right under the warmth" and "trust your child to the big world rather than shrink the world to keep them small."

proposals.proposedText: A steady, warm, practical smile — not denial, but a chosen calm so Keen does not have to carry her fear.
proposals.groundedIn: "smile, and not let him see the tremble" and "holding the feeling so Keen doesn't have to."

proposals.proposedText: When emotion threatens to spill, she returns to a small act of care: smoothing, holding, closing his paws, or making her voice quieter and steadier.
proposals.groundedIn: "When she's moved she does not get louder; she gets quieter and steadier" and "she'll straighten his fur or close his paws around the wristbands."

proposals.proposedText: If caught feeling too much, she does not joke it away; she softens, redirects into a homely action, and lets warmth cover the catch.
proposals.groundedIn: "sensory and homely, never clinical" and "an honest [breath] before the goodbye."

proposals.proposedText: Under pressure she slows down, lowers the voice, and makes the next necessary act tender and exact.
proposals.groundedIn: "Soft, slowed delivery" and "When she's moved she does not get louder; she gets quieter and steadier."

proposals.proposedText: Her pride is bittersweet: warmth first, ache visible underneath, never a clean celebration that erases the cost.
proposals.groundedIn: "the bravest, quietest act a parent ever performs" and "letting him go anyway."

proposals.proposedText: A still home-shape defined by tending hands: the figure Keen moves away from, and emotionally carries with him.
proposals.groundedIn: "The warm hearth Keen carries with him out to sea" and "Hands that tend."

proposals.proposedText: Her stillness should be charged by restraint: the hand lingering on the wristbands, the smile held a beat too long, the breath she takes so Keen does not have to see the tremble.
proposals.groundedIn: "she carries it in the hand that lingers on the wristbands" and "not let him see the tremble."
